items.name: Spec Compliance
items.note: canonicalizes one basename per review-evidence kind (self/spec/code/doubt/plan/external_code) in lib.review_payloads.CANONICAL_PAYLOAD_BASENAMES, enforced by record_review_pass.py at record time; the PR-review classifier (pr_review_generated.py) is deliberately left untouched, per trg-3b206c08's own scope note

items.name: Error Handling
items.note: canonical_basename_error returns None cleanly when a review-type has no canonical kind (plan_internal) or no payload file was given; no new I/O or failure surface introduced

items.name: Security Basics
items.note: no user input parsed insecurely; net effect narrows the ad-hoc-naming surface a future classifier allowlist could otherwise be tricked by — no secrets or auth touched

items.name: Test Quality
items.note: new tests assert real accept/reject outcomes (wrong basename -> exit 2 with the expected name cited; canonical basename -> accepted), not internal state; ~20 existing CLI call sites across 8 test files updated to use the registry instead of ad-hoc names so they exercise the real production shape

items.name: Performance Basics
items.note: a dict lookup and a basename comparison; no loops, no I/O beyond the existing --payload-file read

items.name: Naming & Structure
items.note: registry + validator placed in lib/review_payloads.py (the existing payload-adapter home); record_review_pass.py's own line count was kept at its pre-existing grandfathered ceiling (395) by moving the message-construction there instead of inlining it -- no bloat ratchet

items.name: Affected Boundaries
items.note: Producer = the SKILL-prose-instructed agent writing the raw payload file (iteration-reviews.md/iteration-planning.md/sub-iterate-runner.md, now updated to redirect to the canonical name); Consumer = record_review_pass.py's canonical_basename_error + build_review_evidence. A real round-trip is exercised by the updated CLI tests (write canonical-named file -> CLI reads and accepts it) across 8 test files; touches_io_boundary did not fire for this diff (verified via risk_detectors.is_io_boundary_change against the actual changed-file list), so this round-trip coverage is additional rigor, not a mandatory gate

items.name: Test Hygiene Probe
items.note: scan_test_hygiene.py --diff reports no findings against the changed test files
